  1. Networking and endpoints

Networking and endpoints

Quick local access

Port-forwarding needs no ingress and is the fastest way to verify a model.

kubectl get svc -n models

# Classic InferenceService
kubectl port-forward -n models svc/sentiment-predictor 8080:80

# LLMInferenceService
kubectl port-forward -n models svc/llama-8b 8080:80

Endpoint paths

Workload Path Payload
Predictive InferenceService /v1/models/{name}:predict {"instances": [...]}
Open Inference Protocol /v2/models/{name}/infer {"inputs": [...]}
Generative runtimes /openai/v1/completions OpenAI completion request
Generative runtimes /openai/v1/chat/completions OpenAI chat request
LLMInferenceService /v1/chat/completions OpenAI chat request

Predictive example:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models/fraud-detector:predict \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"instances": [[5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2]]}'

Chat example:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-8b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain vector databases briefly."}],
    "max_tokens": 200,
    "temperature": 0.2
  }'

Streaming:

curl -N http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "llama-8b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Count to ten"}], "stream": true}'

List served models:

curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/models

In-cluster access

Other workloads reach a model through the cluster service name:

http://sentiment-predictor.models.svc.cluster.local/v1/models/sentiment:predict
http://llama-8b.models.svc.cluster.local/v1/chat/completions

Configure an OpenAI-compatible client with:

base_url = http://llama-8b.models.svc.cluster.local/v1
api_key  = not-needed

Ingress for predictive workloads

The core controller owns ingress defaults:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      gateway:
        domain: models.example.com
        urlScheme: https
        ingressGateway:
          enableGatewayApi: true
          className: istio
          kserveGateway: kserve/kserve-ingress-gateway
          createGateway: false

With a domain configured, each model receives a hostname derived from the template:

https://sentiment-models.models.example.com

Adjust the pattern:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      gateway:
        domainTemplate: '{{ .Name }}-{{ .Namespace }}.{{ .IngressDomain }}'
        additionalIngressDomains:
          - internal.example.com

For a non-Istio controller such as Contour, set the class name:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      gateway:
        ingressGateway:
          className: contour

A top-level kserve: block does not reach the subchart. Ingress settings must be under kserve-resources.

Disable ingress creation entirely for internal-only clusters:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      gateway:
        disableIngressCreation: true

Routers for LLM workloads

LLMInferenceService uses a router with three parts:

Part Purpose
gateway Gateway API gateway that accepts traffic
route HTTPRoute binding the gateway to the workload
scheduler LLM-aware endpoint picker for cache- and load-aware routing

The chart default requests all three as managed:

llmDefaults:
  router:
    gateway: {}
    route: {}
    scheduler: {}

Attach to an existing gateway instead of creating one:

llmInferenceServices:
  - name: llama-8b
    model:
      uri: hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
    router:
      gateway:
        refs:
          - name: shared-gateway
            namespace: infrastructure
      route: {}
      scheduler: {}

Service-only exposure, with no gateway or route:

    router:
      scheduler: {}

Several workloads can share one gateway by pointing at the same reference, which keeps a single external address and TLS certificate.

Gateway API prerequisites 

kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io
kubectl get gatewayclass
kubectl get gateway -A
kubectl get httproute -A

Install the Gateway API CRDs and a controller before enabling Gateway-based routing.

TLS

Terminate TLS at the gateway by referencing a certificate Secret in the gateway definition. cert-manager can issue it:

apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: models-tls
  namespace: infrastructure
spec:
  secretName: models-tls
  dnsNames:
    - models.example.com
  issuerRef:
    name: letsencrypt
    kind: ClusterIssuer

The cert-manager instance used by KServe webhooks is separate and is configured under kserve-resources.kserve.certManager.

Restricting traffic

Model endpoints have no built-in authentication. Protect them with network policy, a service mesh, or an authenticating gateway.

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: models-allow-apps
  namespace: models
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: applications

Diagnosing access problems

Symptom Check
Connection refused on port-forward kubectl get pods -n models; the pod may not be ready
404 on a model path Confirm the model name in the URL and in /v1/models
503 from the gateway Workload not ready, or the route points at the wrong service
DNS name does not resolve Verify the gateway address and external DNS records
Works in-cluster, not externally Inspect gateway, HTTPRoute, and load balancer state 
kubectl get inferenceservice -n models -o wide
kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models -o wide
kubectl get httproute -n models -o yaml
kubectl describe gateway -n infrastructure shared-gateway
